A group of researchers has been showing groups of students pictures and have given them a task to find out if students will ask the question “Where did this document or this picture that I'm looking at come from?” when they see claims about their favorite superheroes or a vivid photograph.

Students are shown a picture of daisies along with the claim that the flowers have “nuclear birth defects” from Japan’s Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster. Students may also claim that it cannot be said that the cause of the daisies' unusual {7} is caused by the nuclear radiation. Various drafts of this task were piloted with 454 high school students. The final version was given to 170 high school students. In general, students across grade levels were captivated by the photograph and relied on it to evaluate the trustworthiness of the post. They ignored key details, such as the source of the photo. Less than 20% of students constructed "Mastery" responses, or responses that questioned the origin of the post or the source of the photo.
